claims.text: Conventional AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is produced by gas atomization with a particle-size distribution suitable for LPBF.
LPBF consolidates alloy powder through laser-induced melting and fusion.
Switching from LPBF to room-temperature powder-loaded ink extrusion followed by sintering and silicide coating will reduce residual stress in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed intervention will preserve or enhance the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components relative to LPBF.
The proposed intervention will simplify processing relative to high-thermal-load LPBF.
Sintering AlCrFeNiSi green parts at 600–800 °C will promote diffusion and neck growth without imposing high thermal gradients.
An in situ pack-cementation silicide coating will enhance the surface integrity of the printed and sintered AlCrFeNiSi components.
The applicable ink-extrusion layer thickness is 20–50 µm.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature components with dimensions below approximately 10 mm under ambient-atmosphere processing.
Residual stress, microstructure, and mechanical properties will be evaluated at room temperature by XRD, SEM/TEM, micro-tensile testing, and hardness testing.
Room-temperature ink extrusion and controlled sintering will produce a homogeneous, fine-grained AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The silicide coating will act as both a diffusion barrier and a stress relaxer.
Rapid melting and solidification during LPBF generate residual stresses and microstructural defects.
Avoiding melting during printing will minimize residual stresses and defects by reducing manufacturing thermal cycles and gradients.
Controlled sintering at 600–800 °C will consolidate the parts without high-temperature-induced degradation.
The silicide coating will stabilize surface phases and mitigate oxidation.
Relative to LPBF components, the proposed components will have lower residual stress and better-preserved ductility and tensile strength.
LPBF-produced miniature components have high residual thermal stress, microcracking, and degraded mechanical properties because of rapid melting and solidification.
The proposed processing window should apply to AlCrFeNiSi powders with similar particle-size distributions but may require adjustment for larger components or different alloys.
